text:
Mira: hi all, first day and hitting an odd MDM/FileVault state. Kandji enrollment finished but FileVault shows "Escrow pending" and the login screen still asks for my personal recovery key I generated during setup. device is MBP M2, macOS Ventura 13.6. anyone seen partial escrow like this?
theo-it: welcome Mira! short answer: yes. did you create a personal recovery key (printed string or hardware key) during initial FileVault setup, or did you pick the company recovery option?
Mira: i picked "personal recovery key" because i wanted to attach my YubiKey, then clicked the Kandji invite after logging in. i presume that order might have mattered.
kandji-bot: Kandji last check-in: 2024-11-02T14:21:00Z. Device state: Enrolled. FileVault escrow: pending. Pending actions: push-escrow, verify-protectors.
theo-it: yep, that flow can leave the institutional escrow unset because the device already has an active personal protector. Can you paste output of `sudo fdesetup status`? a quick copy is fine.
Mira: pasted below:
```bash
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users: Mira (Enabled)
Escrow: Escrow pending
```
Mira: also tried System Settings -> FileVault -> Turn Off and Turn On to force re-escrow but it errors complaining about personal key in use.
theo-it: ok. options: 1) we request a temporary admin push and remove the personal recovery key so Kandji can push the institutional key (fastest), 2) you do a reinstall with MDM-first image which guarantees escrow (more time), or 3) we try a manual fdesetup protector management if you want to keep uptime. which do you prefer?
Mira: don't want reinstall. what's involved with manual protector management?
alex-sec: security note: any manual removal of a personal recovery key must be done with IT coordination. If we remove it, we ensure institutional escrow is present immediately and log the operation. Option 1 is fine. Option 3 would require generating a new institutional recovery password locally and escrowing it, which is more error-prone for onboarding.
lena-people: looping HR so the temporary admin action is recorded on your new-hire checklist. :white_check_mark: Mira i'll add a note to ticket ONB-5112.
theo-it: Mira - i'm going to open a temp-admin session and remove the personal recovery key, then force a Kandji keyset push. deploy-bot: temp-admin session created for theo-it (20m). ticket ONB-5112.
Mira: standing by at my desk with YubiKey and a USB-C hub. thanks!
theo-it: done - removed personal recovery protector, instructed Kandji to push escrow. please run `sudo fdesetup status` now.
Mira: re-ran it, shows:
```bash
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users: Mira (Enabled)
Escrow: Institutional recovery key present (Kandji)
```
Mira: restarted and unlocked with my usual password. YubiKey prompt didn't appear at FileVault screen (i think YubiKey is only for login 2FA here?).
theo-it: correct — macOS FileVault unlock will accept the recovery password or enabled user credentials; we don't bind hardware 2FA to the FileVault protector by default. you can still register your YubiKey for login if you'd like.
alex-sec: please re-register your YubiKey in Okta/SSO and confirm that device-level MFA is set. we'll mark escrow verified.
lena-people: onboarding ticket updated and will be closed once Mira confirms SSO 2FA.
Mira: confirmed, YubiKey re-registered for SSO. all good — thanks team! :partyparrot:
theo-it: adding a short doc to onboarding checklist about "If you want to use a personal recovery key + YubiKey, enroll MDM first then enable FileVault" to avoid this race.
Mira: thanks again, appreciate the speedy help.
